item.title: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers: Re: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Good day, Tribal Machination. Welcome to the SCP Wiki!

Glad to see you're interested in writing for the site. Industrial machinery is really cool, and if you ever want to find people who have similar interests, I recommend you check out our IRC chatrooms where you can talk with everyone. Reading around before jumping into writing immediately's a good idea. Particularly, since you plan on becoming an author, you should read a lot of the newer articles to get a feel for what the on-site community is interested in these days. I personally suggest checking out SCP-5762. Anyway, here's some resources that'll help you out around the site:

◎ Open Resources ◎
◉ Close Resources ◉

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts.

Sandbox

For hashing out concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by the community if you need help refining your concept.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out our Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular, recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community.

With that said, I hope your time here is great.

item.title: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers: Re: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hihi my name is flumbles! Ever since I accidentally stumbled on this place in early high school and consequentially had to sleep with a light on for at least 2 weeks I've been a longtime lurker on this place. While the sheer terror from the things I read here has waned, my appreciation for this place hasn't, and I've finally pulled the trigger and made an account.

Ultimately, I'm looking to write and contribute something. I realize that it'll probably be a long long time before I get to finally publishing, but honestly I think I relish that - no doubt I'll learn oodles of good writing advice in the days to come.

I'm also interested in becoming a advisor/topic expert for medical topics (I'm currently a medical student with a BSc in Biomedical Science), but I'm unsure if I'm too new for that for the time being.

Regardless, I'm happy to be here ^_^. Also I like water because I suck at swimming and I feel like waterbending could make that much easier for me.

item.title: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers:
item.content:encoded:
Hello, all!

I'm Nerdspartan. I've been interested in SCP since the day I first saw Youtube videos of people playing SCP-087, and later SCP:Containment Breach. Recently, I've stumbled upon the SCP narrative channel TheVolgun, which made me come back to the Foundation.

I love the SCP way of depicting horror in an apathetic and scientific fashion, and I wondered if I could write my own SCPs eventually. So do expect me to post something in the idea critique soon! I will also attempt to do a few critiques of other people's work if I feel confident.

My hobbies include nerdy things like playing video games and making video games (with Unity and RPGMaker), and occasionally writing fictions.

If I were an element, I'd probably be earth, because I am of calm, assertive and thoughtful nature, and I like to live my life steadily, with few unforeseen changes.

Thank you for reading and long live the Foundation!

item.title: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers: Re: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers
item.content:encoded:
Greetings there, fellow SCP enthusiasts!

I am Seereeni (Seh-re-nii), and after roughly 5 years of knowing about and following the SCP universe, I decided to make an account of my own, and contribute to this wonderful place in whatever way I can.

One of mine own desires is to write an SCP, humanoid at that, which can then by used by everyone here, veteran and newbie, to link together all the SCPs, in one way or another, either for tales, to create new SCPs, to write interesting logs, or to explain something which they find hard to explain.

Hard? Oh yes, that's how a challenge should be.

I am also a writer on Fanfiction, and as far as my readers have commented, I am apparently almost typo-free in my writing. Do you have a tale or SCP you wish someone to look over for typos? Then do contact me, I am more than happy to help.

Lastly, as you have probably noticed, I am very…detailed in my explanations. This is, naturally, a good thing for a writer, but less so for an SCP Foundation member, something I am very much aware of. I have read the rules and I know that an SCP page should be professional and not use more words than needed. I will try my best to abide by these rules.

With that said, I still have a hard time understanding how this site works. So many links directing one to other links, then to other links…sigh. I barely know how Discord works.

Thus, to all of you veterans who have taken it upon themselves to answer newbie questions….I pity you, and I am sorry. I'll try to learn fast and keep your suffering minimal.

Kay bye.

item.title: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers: Re: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers
item.content:encoded:
Salutations one and all,
I go by JoysticKnight (I imagine you could shorten that to Jsk if it's a little much to type out).

I tend to be an avid enthusiast of design. I like to break apart the inner workings of all this world has to offer. Be it science, psychology, philosophy, art, traditional/video-games, or music to name a few large topics. Although, I do have a particular affinity towards music analysis, and game design.

As far as the foundation is concerned, I've seen it's growth over the years with the wealth of it's library and the troves of content people make concerning it. I indeed have adored the vast imagination of it's machinations showing thoroughly no true limit to the vastness of this world. And it's by this merit I have finally grown enough gall to even consider joining.

Personally speaking I tend to be a shelled and hermit-like in nature. So forgive me if it takes some time to flourish in any way. I have something of a social life, but tend to not act upon it, so participating in a forum or collective source is a rather new experience for me.

I hope that as time marches on I am able to contribute in some forward manner, gaining people's trust and flame of curiousity. Until then, I am but still just another peer.

Also I obvisouly don't talk with this much grandure in real life, it's just nice every once in a while to really convey the right emotions with fitting words.

So about that question. I suppose I'll go with water, it's an endlessly malleable substance that we learn does something new every 5 years or so. I admire it's ability to function and create function.

item.title: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers: Re: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello there, name's Ascentimber, and I'm… here now, I guess.

I have heard of the SCP series since… maybe 2012? 2013? But I was only aware of it as an actual community and not just stories in 2016 or so. I guess I have lurked for some time after, but have just recently found the drive to contribute.

Personally, I have no ideas for SCPs as of yet, but I do plan to write on other things. My main interest here is to actually help the Indonesian SCP translation branch, but I will most likely still write something here. I am doing a lot of independent historical research as of the past year or so, so anything I write will probably be based on history.

If there's anything I would like to ask to any staff members that might reply to my introduction message is: 1. What are the current steps on writing SCPs? and, 2. What are the current steps on writing for the Log of Anomalous Items/Extranormal Events/Unexplained Locations?

Answering the random question, it's probably water. Probably because it's the least mismatching one of 'em all.

Anyhow, I would also like to thank the staffs for the acceptance, and a quick one too. It's almost instantaneous, I would say, unlike the two or three day period that the guide says will take.
